- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Running a large language model on a blockchain network would likely be less efficient than on a centralized system due to the decentralized nature of blockchain networks.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The energy consumption of blockchain networks, especially those using proof-of-work consensus algorithms, is significantly higher than centralized systems.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] While advances in blockchain technology could make it feasible to run a large language model on a blockchain network, it is currently impractical and challenging with significant limitations in performance and energy consumption.
- [USER] Asked how many years it would take for the fastest blockchain to catch up to the TPS (transactions per second) requirements of a large language model.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] It is difficult to predict how many years it would take for the fastest blockchain to meet the TPS requirements of a large language model.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The fastest public blockchain networks can process a few hundred transactions per second, while a large language model would likely require thousands or millions of TPS.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Current fast blockchains include Solana (over 65,000 TPS), EOSIO (over 4,000 TPS), and Algorand (over 1,000 TPS).
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Private blockchains like Chain and Hyperledger Fabric can also process thousands of transactions per second.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] TPS numbers are approximate and may vary based on specific implementations and resources available on the network.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Other important factors for running a large language model on a blockchain include computational resources, storage capacity, and network latency.
